paper.title_en: On co-dimension 2 defect anomalies in N=4 SYM and (2,0) theory via brane probes in AdS/CFT
paper.abstract_en: We consider a half-BPS solution for a D3 brane probe in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ that has world-volume geometry of AdS$_3 \times S^1$. It intersects the boundary over a surface that represents a dimension 2 defect in the boundary ${\cal N}=4$ SYM theory. The effective action of the probe brane is proportional to the logarithmically divergent volume of AdS$_3$ and may thus be interpreted as computing conformal anomaly of supersymmetric $S^2$ defect. The classical action scales as $N$. We compute the 1-loop correction to it due to quantum fluctuations of the D3 brane world-volume fields and compare the result to an earlier suggested expression for the defect anomaly. With the boundary condition for the zero mode of the world-volume vector required by supersymmetry the sum over the modes gives the 1-loop coefficient $-3$ instead of the expected $-6$. We suggest that the remaining part is due to the classical response of the background to the probe. We also perform a similar analysis of a half-BPS supersymmetric M5 brane probe solution in AdS$_7 \times S^4$ with the world-volume geometry of AdS$_5 \times S^1$ that represents a dimension 4 defect in the boundary (2,0) 6d theory. Here the classical M5 brane action computes the leading order $N^2$ term in $a$-anomaly of the supersymmetric $S^4$ defect. The fluctuations form a tower of chiral multiplets and a flavour current multiplet of the 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal symmetry. We perform a detailed computation of the 1-loop correction to the M5 brane effective action and discuss prescription dependence of the prediction for the contribution to the $S^4$ defect $a$-anomaly coefficient.
